title: Hierarchical ODE: Learning Continuous-Time Physical Prototypes for Early Link Failure Detection
claim: Our continuous-time model yields a clean hierarchy whose subtrees fall below the cut-off as coherent clusters; discrete baselines do not.
layout: 5 dendrogram panels in a 3+2 grid, shared red dashed cut-off line
description: Five dendrogram subplots are arranged in two rows, with three on top (ODE, ModernTCN, ResNet) and two below (LSTM, GRU). Each plot has a y-axis called Normalized Distance running from 0 to 1.0. The x-axis is Sample Index. Tree branches are gray above the threshold. Branches below it are colored red, blue, orange or green to mark clusters. A red dashed horizontal line marks the same adaptive cut-off in every panel. In the ODE panel, a few compact colored subtrees sit below the line, which gives clear, well-separated prototypes. ModernTCN and ResNet have many fragmented, tall branches that cross the line. LSTM and GRU show a few colored clusters, but some are merged unevenly. The eye goes first to the ODE panel at top left, then compares the cut-off across panels.
caption: {Hierarchical Structure of Prototypes.} The dendrogram reveals the semantic grouping of latent dynamics, where the red dashed line denotes the {adaptive cut-off threshold}. Sub-trees merging below this threshold are identified as coherent physical prototypes.
abstract: Time series prototype learning is fundamentally challenged by observational ambiguity. Discrete architectures fail to resolve this, as they lack the capacity to decouple stochastic noise from continuous dynamics. Furthermore, rigid closed-set assumptions fail to capture unseen diversity. To address these limitations, we propose a hierarchical ordinary differential equation clustering network, which utilizes neural ordinary differential equation to model latent state evolution as a continuous integral curve. This formulation enforces temporal continuity to effectively disentangle smooth feature trends from stochastic noise, while our adaptive hierarchical mechanism autonomously determines the appropriate number of prototypes without rigid prior constraints. Validated on the early link failure detection task with irregularly sampled time series, the proposed method effectively extracts underlying physical prototypes, thereby enabling robust failure detection. Our code is available at https://github.com/NJ-LNN/Hierarchical-ODE.
